A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PGW formulation and Frank–Wolfe solvers despite the changed title and substantial expansion. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original solver runtimes, synthetic shape-matching experiments, and positive-unlabeled learning accuracies and timings in Section 5 and Appendix L.

after.justification: v2 reports original outlier matching, shape retrieval, and barycenter interpolation results, alongside retained and revised runtime and positive-unlabeled learning experiments.

M1.justification: The original PGW objective and two solvers are largely retained, but Section 5.3 and Appendix M introduce barycenter optimization, alternating coupling/matrix updates, and a mass-constrained variant in Algorithms 3–4. The pruning text also changes from rows containing no negative entries to rows containing a nonnegative entry; this documents an inconsistent rule without establishing an implementation change.

E1.justification: v2 adds two shape-retrieval datasets and noisy shape-interpolation tasks. It replaces the square/circle-to-cube/sphere mixture-matching experiment with moon and circle–sphere matching under outlier contamination. MNIST, EMNIST, Caltech Office PU learning, and the synthetic solver-timing task remain.

E2.justification: Existing distance and solver comparator families remain, with primal-PGW renamed MPGW. The substantive extension is evaluating GW barycenters against PGW barycenters in the new interpolation experiments, Figures 3 and 5. The MPGW barycenter algorithm is introduced but is not shown as an evaluated interpolation baseline.

E3.justification: v2 introduces random-representative nearest-neighbor classification, stratified 10-fold kernel-SVM evaluation, and SMACOF reconstruction of barycenters. Table 3 adds PU timing configurations with 2,000 source and 10,000 target samples, beyond the retained 1,000/5,000 configuration. Cross-feature POT-initialized comparisons are dropped. Interpolation settings contain an unresolved discrepancy: Appendix M.1 says 0.5% noise where Section 5.3 and Figure 5 say 5%.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled outlier tests for matching and interpolation robustness across three spatial noise distributions and two figure-labeled noise levels, 5% and 10%. Figure 5 includes noise overlapping the signal region, where the methods behave more similarly. Retrieval confusion matrices also expose class-specific errors. These analyses are absent from v1.

E5.justification: Section 5.2 newly specifies 10,000 randomized representative-selection repetitions and reports SVM accuracy averaged across 10 folds. These are new repetition and aggregation practices, not evidence of additional runs for retained experiments. Neither version provides seed identities, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds retrieval results, including PGW accuracies of 96.25% and 100% versus GW's 98.13% and 80.83%, plus new matching and interpolation findings. PU timings and Caltech Office accuracies change: POT-initialized PGW on SURF(A) to SURF(A) changes from 100% to 74.7% in v1 Table 3 versus v2 Table 4. Digit accuracies remain unchanged. Additional timing rows are reported; differing hardware descriptions preclude treating revised runtimes as clean performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: v1 Proposition 3.4's transport-cost cutoff and its proof are removed. The metric proof is substantially rewritten using three auxiliary points and an untruncated cost, with explicit compact-space and equivalence assumptions. v2 also develops Lipschitz-based existence arguments, proves the large-penalty PGW-to-GW limit, formalizes the relationship with MPGW, and derives barycenter updates. These exceed renumbering or expanded explanation.

C1.justification: v1 already claims that PGW defines a metric, but emphasizes efficient solvers. v2 newly claims the first GW-based metric for non-probability metric measure spaces, introduces barycenters as a contribution, and adds principal claims about shape discrimination and robustness in interpolation. The original solver contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 attributes retrieval behavior to metric discrimination and some UGW behavior to Sinkhorn regularization. It qualifies interpolation advantages under overlapping noise and explains that MDS requires manual orientation alignment because GW/PGW are invariant to rotations and reflections. Appendix Q expands the line-search limitation, although disabling line search for PU learning was already disclosed in v1.

D1.justification: v2 documents new preprocessing and implementation settings, including k-means with 1,024 centers, SVM kernel scale 10, barycenter iteration limits and tolerances, and task-specific mass and penalty choices. It specifies a PU penalty bound where v1 only requested a sufficiently large value, adds dataset-access directions, and revises the hardware description to an EPYC 7713, 256 GB RAM, and one RTX A6000 rather than v1's four-GPU description.

R1.justification: v2 expands positioning from providing solvers to distinguishing a claimed metric from existing unbalanced discrepancies. New Appendix L develops the comparison with Chapel et al.'s mass-constrained formulation, including non-equivalence and a distinguishing example. Added references cover robust optimal transport, metric geometry, and linear GW; the change is substantive beyond citation additions.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and contribution narrative are extensively rewritten around the metric. Solver 2 and its conversion result move into Appendix G; runtime and PU experiments move into Appendices O and P. Background and proof exposition are reorganized, and primal-PGW terminology becomes MPGW throughout.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the original matching illustration, adds retrieval distance/confusion matrices and interpolation grids, and introduces barycenter algorithm displays. The runtime figure moves to Appendix O and is redrawn. PU tables separate initialization method from accuracy/time and add displays for expanded timing results. The original t-SNE visualization is retained as Figure 10.

improvement.justification: The revised metric argument, derived barycenter procedure, and controlled retrieval and contamination experiments substantially improve support for PGW's mathematical role and practical usefulness beyond v1's solver-focused demonstrations. More implementation detail and explicit MDS limitations improve assessability. New defects remain, notably the pruning wording and inconsistencies in Appendix M's interpolation equation and noise level, but they do not outweigh the substantial gains in justification and validation.
